tagline: The riverside capital of golden spires and heavy history — royal palaces, Khmer Rouge memorials, and the gateway to Angkor.
overview: Phnom Penh sits where the Mekong, Bassac and Tonlé Sap rivers meet — the 'four faces' the city is named for. The Royal Palace's golden spires and the Silver Pagoda rise over a riverside promenade that fills with dancers at sunset.

The city asks visitors to remember: the Tuol Sleng museum (a school turned Khmer Rouge prison) and the Choeung Ek killing fields confront the 1975–79 genocide that emptied the city. It's sobering, essential context — and it makes the country's warmth hit harder.
Speed's 2024 tour streamed from Phnom Penh. The city is also the practical gateway — most travellers continue to Siem Reap for Angkor Wat's temple mountains.

funFacts.title: FOUR FACES
funFacts.text: The city sits at the chaktomuk — the 'four faces' junction of three rivers.

funFacts.title: SILVER PAGODA
funFacts.text: The palace temple's floor is laid with over 5,000 silver tiles.

funFacts.title: THE KILLING FIELDS
funFacts.text: Choeung Ek and Tuol Sleng memorialise the Khmer Rouge genocide.

funFacts.title: A CITY EMPTIED
funFacts.text: The Khmer Rouge evacuated all of Phnom Penh in 1975 — it was a ghost town for years.

funFacts.title: REVERSED RIVER
funFacts.text: The Tonlé Sap river reverses direction each monsoon — a unique hydrology.

funFacts.title: WAT PHNOM
funFacts.text: The hilltop temple named for founding grandmother Penh is the city's origin legend.

funFacts.title: FRENCH COLONIAL
funFacts.text: Art Deco Central Market's yellow dome dates to 1937.

funFacts.title: THE ANGKOR GATEWAY
funFacts.text: Siem Reap and Angkor Wat are a short flight or bus away.

funFacts.title: TUK-TUK CAPITAL
funFacts.text: Remork tuk-tuks are the transport of choice — cheap and everywhere.

funFacts.title: RIVERSIDE NIGHTS
funFacts.text: The Sisowath Quay promenade fills with families and street food at dusk.

faq.q: What is the population of Phnom Penh?
faq.a: The greater Phnom Penh area is home to about 2,300,000 people.

faq.q: What is Phnom Penh famous for?
faq.a: Phnom Penh is famous for the Royal Palace and riverside, the sobering Khmer Rouge memorials, and the gateway to Angkor Wat.
